verdict.line: You win by taunting Nasus off his Q farm before level 6 and itemizing antiheal into Soul Eater; you lose if you let him free-farm into a stacked Fury of the Sands and still try to trade into it.

brief.thesis: Nasus's entire power curve is gated by uncontested last-hits on Q (Siphoning Strike), and Shen's E (Shadow Dash) taunts any enemy champion it dashes through — which means Shen can turn Nasus's own farming animation into a free trade. The data backs this: Shen holds a 52.3% win rate over 1442 games with both the lane and solo-kill edge, though the shape is listed as even because Nasus eventually out-scales any lane he isn't denied in.

theirWindow.when: level 6+, Fury of the Sands up
theirWindow.what: Nasus's R (Fury of the Sands), 120s cooldown, range 400, gives him bonus health, attack range and cast range while draining nearby enemies' max health into bonus damage for the duration. If he pops it and walks up, do not stand and trade — back off and let the turret and minions eat it, since OP.GG's own read on this matchup is that your turret dies fast if you've already left lane after 6.

yourWindow.when: any time he's mid-last-hit on a caster minion
yourWindow.what: Shen's E (Shadow Dash), cooldown 16/14/12/10/8s, range 575, dashes him to a location and taunts every enemy champion he passes through while dealing minor damage. Dash through Nasus while he's animation-locked on Q (Siphoning Strike) to taunt him off the minion, then stack Q (Vorpal Blade) autos and W (Feint) to soak the retaliation.

start.why: Nasus's early trades are all auto-attack poke from Q (Siphoning Strike); the flat damage reduction and sustain from Doran's Shield (52.3% over 1112 games, 59.9% pick) lets you hold the taunt-engage pattern without losing the lane-sustain war.

boots.why: Nasus's whole kit is auto-attack damage once he's stacking Q; Plated Steelcaps (52.2% over 1120 games, 64.2% pick) directly cuts that down rather than trading for tenacity he can't apply much CC with anyway.

core.why: gives you the wave-clear and sustained damage to actually punish his farm windows instead of just shoving him off CS for free
core tank-damage hybrid component on the highest-winrate path (56.5% over 154 games) into this matchup
Nasus's passive Soul Eater is bonus lifesteal — Thornmail's grievous wounds directly undercuts the one resource that lets him win extended all-ins

situational.when: he's already snowballing Q stacks and you need antiheal online before full Thornmail finishes
his stacked autos and Fury of the Sands damage drain are the thing actually killing you late
their comp has burst magic damage layered on top of his sustained physical pressure
your team wants more utility/peel out of you than raw tank stats

runes.keystoneWhy: Grasp rewards the exact pattern you're running — taunt in, land an extra auto on Nasus, heal off it — and it's the highest-pick-rate page for this matchup (55.2% win rate, 37.6% pick)

summoners.why: Flash+Ignite is both the most-picked (73.3%) and highest-winrate (52.8%) spell combo here, and Ignite's burn directly cuts the Soul Eater lifesteal Nasus leans on to win extended trades — exactly what OP.GG's own tip flags as the deciding factor in this lane.

playing.title: Taunt him off his farm
playing.detail: Dash E (Shadow Dash) through Nasus while he's mid-Q (Siphoning Strike) on a minion. The taunt locks him in place and denies the stack, which is the single biggest thing you can do to this champion before level 6.

playing.title: Track his Wither cooldown
playing.detail: Nasus's W (Wither), cooldown 15/14/13/12/11s, range 700, decelerates your move and attack speed over time. Don't pop W (Feint) before it lands — save the shield for after he's committed, since a wasted Feint into Wither just extends the slow's punish window.

playing.title: Step off Spirit Fire immediately
playing.detail: Nasus's E (Spirit Fire), flat 12s cooldown, range 650, drops a zone that deals damage and strips armor from anyone standing in it. It's not a one-time hit — walk out the instant it lands rather than trying to last-hit through it.

playing.title: Use Q to offset his chip
playing.detail: Q (Vorpal Blade), cooldown 6/5.5/5/4.5/4s, range 475, damages the target and heals allies who attack it afterward. Fire it into every trade window so your own sustain keeps pace with his passive lifesteal.

playing.title: Respect a readied Fury of the Sands
playing.detail: Once his R (Fury of the Sands) is up at level 6+, he gets bonus health, attack range, and a max-health drain on anyone nearby for the duration. Don't stand and trade into that — disengage and let it go to waste on minions or turret.

playing.title: Weigh every R roam against your turret
playing.detail: Stand United (R), cooldown 200/180/160/160/160s, global range, shields and teleports you to an ally — but OP.GG's own read on this matchup is that your turret falls fast if you've used it to leave lane after level 6. Only roam when the wave and turret plates can afford it.

brief.patchCaveat: All win rates, pick rates, item paths, runes, and summoner spells above are measured from live games on the current patch via OP.GG; the mechanical reasoning — why the taunt-farm interaction and antiheal timing matter — is my own read on top of that data.

stats.opponentTip: Engage whenever Nasus tries to farm with [Q] and Grasp of the Undying. Purchase items that reduce healing to deal more damage. Your turret can be easily destroyed if you use [R] to leave lane after reaching level 6.
